claims.text: Surface-mediated magnetic domain dynamics significantly control the sharpness of the magnetocaloric response in as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi ribbons.
Surface-mediated magnetic domain dynamics significantly control magnetocaloric hysteresis in these ribbons.
A thin conformal oxide coating modifies the alloy's local surface energy.
A thin conformal oxide coating induces interfacial strain at the coating/alloy interface.
The coating perturbs local surface magnetic anisotropy.
Coating-induced changes in surface energy, strain, and anisotropy facilitate smoother magnetic-domain nucleation.
The interfacial changes reduce domain-wall pinning and facilitate domain-wall motion.
Reduced domain-wall pinning produces a more gradual magnetostructural transformation.
An optimized oxide coating reduces hysteretic loss relative to an uncoated ribbon.
An optimized oxide coating broadens the magnetocaloric entropy-change profile relative to an uncoated ribbon.
Coating the ribbon may improve its effective surface-to-volume ratio and thereby enhance heat-exchange efficiency during magnetic-cooling cycles.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi ribbons have an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure.
The uncoated ribbons exhibit a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The uncoated ribbons exhibit pronounced hysteretic magnetocaloric behavior.
Atomic layer deposition below 150 °C avoids altering the alloy's bulk phase.
The proposed coating effects are expected to apply to ordered-hexagonal, as-deposited ribbons under low applied magnetic fields.
The magnitude of the response may depend on coating thickness and coating material.
Surface-coating effects may be subtle when bulk magnetostructural behavior dominates.
The controlled intervention is to compare uncoated ribbons with ribbons carrying approximately 5 nm and 10 nm ALD oxide coatings.
The surface-mediated explanation is falsified if coating variations produce neither a statistically significant hysteresis reduction nor a change in domain dynamics relative to the uncoated control.
